newsitem.title: UK: UK delivered grain market easier in active trade.
newsitem.headline: UK delivered grain market easier in active trade.

text.p: UK delivered grain brokers reported active trading on Wednesday with consumers, merchants and farmers involved.
Traders said there were a number of factors working together with merchants appearing to dump nearby material while farmers were more willing to sell.

"Most people seem to think the market is going to come a lot lower in the near future and merchants seem to be clearing out their nearby material to buy cheaper grain later on. Farmers are trying to get the best price they can," said one trader.
Traders said consumers were were not chasing the market but were buying material and then pulling back 0.50 stg.
"Consumers are buying, pulling back 0.50 stg and waiting for the sellers to come to them, but we now appear to have reached a point beyond which sellers won't go, for now," said another trader.
"We've had a good day, but I woundn't start jumping for joy yet," one trader said.
February feed wheat in East Anglia traded from 97.50 down to 96 stg, depending on area while in the Avon range 97 stg was paid.
In Yorkshire and East Devon the lowest prices paid for Feb so far is 96.50 stg.
Further forward around 100 to 99.50 stg has been paid for Apr/Jun in most areas.
Feed barley for Jan in west Norfolk and Suffolk has traded at 97.50 stg.
Only one milling wheat 11 percent protein trade was reported when 115.25 stg was paid in the London area for Jan.
Traders reported no actvity on the fob market.
